```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

workDir="/Users/waweru/Documents/2022/IBSpy_Targets/2024-06-03_Rht1_locus/2024-06-08_CS_4B-30860000-30910000_Rht-B1/2025-03-05_ibspy_analysis/"

setwd(paste0(workDir))

kmersPresAbsKmersum <-paste0(workDir,"RhtB1_presence_absence_v2+kmersums.csv")

kmerSeqsRawCounts <- paste0(workDir,"RhtB1_combinedRaWKmerCounts.csv")
```

#### load libraries
```{r}
library(magrittr)
library(tidyverse)
#install.packages("vegan")
library(vegan)
library(readxl)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggplot2)
```



### Import raw data

Load file with combined presence absence for all three intervals.

```{r import-data-presabse-with-kmersums}

pres_abs_kmersums_df_all <- read_csv(kmersPresAbsKmersum, col_names = T)
pres_abs_kmersums_df_all$...1 <- NULL

```

### Accession 1: Chinese and Jagger

Get presence absence data for kmers from either chinese spring (wild type) or jagger (alternate, daruma derived)

```{r}
pres_abs_kmersums_df <- pres_abs_kmersums_df_all %>% filter((grepl("chinese", seqname) | grepl("jagger", seqname))) #81,579


```



```{r immport-data-kmerseq-raw-counts}

kmer_counts_df <- read_csv(kmerSeqsRawCounts, col_names = T)
kmer_counts_df$`Unnamed: 0` <- NULL 
kmer_counts_df$...1 <- NULL

```

Add raw kmer counts to presence absence df, keeping only the rows from the kmer counts file that have corresponding ids in the pre_absence file,with raw kmer counts greater than `1` and less than `255`, and keeping only

```{r merge-files}

presabs_kmersums_raw_counts_df <- left_join(kmer_counts_df, pres_abs_kmersums_df, by = "seqname")

presabs_kmersums_raw_counts_df %<>% filter(raw_kmer_count > 1 & raw_kmer_count <= 255)

```


```{r import-blast-data}

blastInfo <- read_csv(blastOut, col_names = T)
blastInfo$...1 <- NULL
#blastInfo <- blastInfo %>% extract(query_id, into = c("query_id", "interval"),regex = "^((?:[^-]*-){5}[^-]*)-(.*)$" )

```

Add blast info

```{r, add-blast-info}
# merge the above df with the blast df based on kmer ID
by <- join_by(seqname == query_id)

preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf <- left_join(presabs_kmersums_raw_counts_df, blastInfo, by )

```



Create a file with kmersums and raw counts before running the blast to combine to clustered data
```{r}
KmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf_inforDf <- preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf[,c(1,2,3,c(979:ncol(preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf)))]

```

Remove any rows that do not have a raw kmer count

```{r}
preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf %<>% filter(!is.na(raw_kmer_count))
```

Remove any rows that have a kmersum value of 0, for this region we need a few to send use as nulls in our analysis, hence we save them in a file

```{r}
preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf  %>% filter(kmer_sum == 0) -> kmer_sum_0_df

write_csv(kmer_sum_0_df, file = "./RhtB1_NullKmers.csv")

preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf %<>% filter(kmer_sum != 0)
```


Plot the raw kmercounts against the kmersums
  
```{r}

preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf  %>% filter(raw_kmer_count > 1) %>%
  ggplot(.,aes(x=raw_kmer_count, y=kmer_sum)) +
  geom_point()
```

lots of kmers present in almost all the samples

```{r}

preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf %>% 
  ggplot(.,aes(x=raw_kmer_count, y=kmer_sum)) +
  geom_point() +
    ggtitle("Plot of kmerSums against rawCount of kmers from Chinese Spring and Jagger for Rht-B1 locus")

```


Moving on to cluster the accessions based on the kmers
```{r filt-data}

clustering_df <- preAbsKmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf  

clustering_df <- clustering_df[,c(1,4:((ncol(clustering_df))-18))] # with blast infor in the df

#clustering_df <- clustering_df[,c(1,5:((ncol(clustering_df))-5))]

kmer_IDs <- clustering_df$seqname

rownames(clustering_df) <- clustering_df$seqname # set kmerID as row names

clustering_df$seqname <- NULL

clustering_df <- as.data.frame(clustering_df)
rownames(clustering_df) <- kmer_IDs

#str(clustering_df)

#dropping any non numeric columns

clustering_df <- clustering_df[sapply(clustering_df, is.numeric)]
```


Generate a dissimilarity matrix

```{r}

# Step 1: Calculate a dissimilarity matrix
# Use a binary distance measure suitable for presence-absence data.
# "jaccard" is a common choice for binary data.
dissimilarity_matrix <- vegdist(clustering_df, method = "jaccard")

# Step 2: Perform hierarchical clustering
# Use the `hclust` function for hierarchical clustering
hc_clustering_df <- hclust(dissimilarity_matrix, method = "average")

# Step 3: Plot the dendrogram
#plot(hc_clustering_df, main = "Hierarchical Clustering Dendrogram",  sub = "", cex = 0.8)


# Optional: Cut the dendrogram to create clusters
# You can cut the dendrogram at a certain height to form clusters.
#clusters <- cutree(hc_mace, k = 4)  # Adjust k for the number of clusters you want
#print(clusters)


# Step 4: Use pheatmap to plot the heatmap with dendrogram
pheatmap_clustering_df <- pheatmap(
  mat = as.matrix(clustering_df),       # Convert the dataframe to a matrix for pheatmap
  cluster_rows = hc_clustering_df,           # Use the previously calculated hclust for rows
  cluster_cols = TRUE,         # By default, it will cluster columns
  show_rownames = FALSE,        # Show row names (samples)
  fontsize_row = 6,
  show_colnames = FALSE,        # Show column names (variables)
  main =  "Heatmap with Dendrogram of Rht-B1 kmers from Chinese Spring and Jagger",
  filename = "RhtB1_kmer_heatmap.pdf",
  width = 12,
  height = 9
)

```



After generating the heatmap, extract the data based on the order of columns  and rows as they were clustered 

```{r}
# Extract the order of columns after clustering
col_order <- pheatmap_clustering_df$tree_col$order
ordered_colnames <- colnames(clustering_df)[col_order]

# Extract the order of rows after clustering
row_order <- pheatmap_clustering_df$tree_row$order
ordered_rownames <- rownames(clustering_df)[row_order]

# Reorder the data based on the clustering results
# First, reorder the rows and then the columns
clustered_data <- clustering_df[ordered_rownames, ordered_colnames]

# Add the ordered row names as a new column to the reordered data
clustered_data$Clustered_Row_Names <- ordered_rownames

# Optional: Move the new column to the front of the dataframe
clustered_data <- clustered_data[, c(ncol(clustered_data), 1:(ncol(clustered_data) - 1))]

# Print the final clustered data
#print(clustered_data)

## before saving, merge with the kmerSumsFile so we can get the sequences for alignment later

#first rename clustered_row_names column to seqname for merging
# Rename column 'A' to 'X'
#df <- df %>% rename(X = A)
clustered_data <- clustered_data %>% rename(seqname = Clustered_Row_Names)

#clustered_data <- left_join(clustered_data, kmer_counts_kmersums_infor_df,by = "seqname")

#write_csv(clustered_data, file = "./MG_WATDE0776_kmers_seq_clustered.csv")

#===== if we have blast info ====================
#================================================

clustered_data <- left_join(clustered_data, KmerSmsRwCntsBlstDf_inforDf,by = "seqname")

# because we have several contigs, we first arrange by adjusted start, then by contig

clustered_data_srtd <- clustered_data %>% arrange(subject_id, adjusted_start)

#clustered_data_srtd <- clustered_data[order(clustered_data$adjusted_start),]

clustered_dataT <- t(clustered_data_srtd) %>% as.data.frame(.)

clustered_dataT$headers <- rownames(clustered_dataT)

write_csv(clustered_dataT, file = "./2026-Nov_Rht-B1_kmers_seq_clustered_v3.csv")

write_csv(clustered_data_srtd, file = "./2026-Nov_Rht-B1_kmers_seq_clustered_notTransposed.csv")

```
